svg.title: Give each process only the authority it needs
svg.desc: Five gates read top to bottom. 1, separate maintenance from runtime: operator maintenance uses runtime.env plus the migration URL for schema and bootstrap work, while the API uses nonowner application and catalog logins from api-container.env or runtime.env without the migration URL. 2, separate native execution from remote work: the native executor uses native-container.env with database access, release and secret grants, while a remote worker uses worker.env with an API token, release and effect settings and no database authority. 3, verify the token's issuer, keys, audience and client, and resolve an active linked principal. 4, check the current scoped grant for the operation, scope and exact resource or release; a platform administrator link alone does not grant business data. 5, resolve a connector credential separately, from the connection's secretRef through execution authority and a scoped handle grant to the secret provider, in the executing process only, with destination and egress policy still applying. A private env file never bypasses authorization.
svg.text: Give each process only the authority it needs
Configuration selects credentials. Each operation still checks the caller and
its scope.
READ DOWN • Each arrow carries the result into the next step
1. Separate maintenance from runtime
Operator maintenance uses runtime.env plus the migration URL
for explicit schema/bootstrap work.
API uses nonowner application and catalog logins; runtime
excludes the migration URL.
CONFIGURATION • API uses api-container.env or runtime.env
2. Separate native execution from remote work
Native executor uses native-container.env: app/catalog DB
access, release and secret grants.
Remote SDK worker uses worker.env: API token, release, and
effect settings, with no orchestration DB authority.
PROCESS • A remote worker claims through the API
3. Verify the token and resolve the identity
Check the trusted issuer and signing keys, the audience,
and the client. Then resolve the linked local principal
and require it to be active.
IDENTITY • A token is the start of the check
4. Check the current scoped grant
Authorize the operation, scope, and exact resource or release.
A platform administrator link alone does not grant
business-data access.
AUTHORITY • The grant must still be current
5. Resolve a connector credential separately
Connection secretRef → execution authority → scoped handle
grant → secret provider.
Only the executing process resolves the value; destination and
egress policy still apply.
SECRET • Do not pass resolved values through workflow input
Keep configuration ownership explicit
A private env file does not bypass authorization. Use the right identity for
the process and the exact scope for each operation.

g.text: Give each process the identity and credentials its own job requires.
